observation_summary: The RegulaFalsiSolver fails to converge for certain functions, resulting in an infinite loop or exhaustion of evaluations because the update formula repeatedly produces the same value due to limited double precision.
hypothesis: The implementation of the Regula Falsi algorithm was attempting to handle stagnation by manually forcing an update to the bounds when the new value matched the old one. This modification was flawed, as it interfered with the mathematical properties of the algorithm and failed to resolve the convergence issue effectively, leading to an infinite loop.
prediction: Removing the problematic logic that attempts to force an update when x == x1 will restore the standard Regula Falsi behavior, which, while slow, avoids the incorrect state manipulation that caused the infinite loop/evaluation exhaustion.
experiment_rationale: The fix removes the conditional block that was attempting to force an update to x0 and f0 when x == x1. This confirms that the logic was an incorrect attempt to patch the algorithm's inherent convergence limitations, and its removal is the correct fix to prevent the erroneous state.
reasoning_summary: The bug is an algorithmic issue where the implementation attempted to 'fix' the slow convergence of the Regula Falsi method by manually modifying the bounds when stagnation occurred. This modification was incorrect and caused the solver to fail. The fix involves removing this flawed procedural logic, which is a classic correction of an algorithmic step.
evidence_used: The fix diff shows the removal of an 'if (x == x1)' block that was modifying x0 and f0.
The bug report comments explicitly state that the problem was due to the update formula giving the same value and that the 'fix' was an attempt to modify the algorithm to avoid failure.
The discussion confirms that the modification was not a standard Regula Falsi implementation and was causing issues.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves removing an 'if' condition, the root cause is not a missing guard, but an incorrect algorithmic strategy to handle stagnation.
This is a local procedural correction to an existing algorithm, not a design-level capability gap.
